risks: Minimal: secondary use of programme records. The main risk is re-identification of patients in small rural subgroups, handled by suppressing cells under five.
consent: Waiver of consent granted for secondary use (REB-2026-331); a notice on the programme's web page explains the analysis and how to opt out.
data: Access under IG-CR-2026-19; postcodes are converted to deprivation quintile and distance and then deleted; the analysis file is pseudonymised and kept on the hospital research server.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: women, older people, people in deprived areas and rural patients are the groups most likely to be failed by either setting; completion and uptake are reported for each, and the board is told whether a remote default would leave any group worse off.
effectiveness: The comparison informs the default programme; it cannot show that remote rehabilitation causes higher or lower completion.
partnerships: Rehabilitation staff, the information governance office, and two patient partners (one who completed remotely, one who stopped).
rebPath: Research ethics board waiver of consent for secondary use (REB-2026-331) and information governance approval (IG-CR-2026-19) are both in place.
limitations: Confounding by choice; employment and car access unrecorded; one programme.
summary: Secondary use under a consent waiver, with small-cell suppression and equity reporting.
